projects.readme:
# NODE - Northern Ontario Dev Exchange

Official website for NODE Sudbury - a community-driven tech org based in Greater Sudbury, Ontario.

**Live site:** [node-sudbury.vercel.app](https://node-sudbury.vercel.app) *(custom domain coming soon)*
**Dev preview:** [node-sudbury-dev.vercel.app](https://node-sudbury-dev.vercel.app)

---

## Local Setup

**Requirements:** Node.js 18+, npm

```bash
git clone https://github.com/NODE-Sudbury/NODE-Sudbury.github.io.git
cd NODE-Sudbury.github.io
npm install
npm run dev
```

Runs at `http://localhost:3000`.

---

## Tech Stack

- [Next.js 14](https://nextjs.org) - App Router
- [Tailwind CSS](https://tailwindcss.com)
- [Supabase](https://supabase.com) - Auth and database
- [Vercel](https://vercel.com) - Hosting and preview deployments

---

## Contributing

NODE is open to everyone - no experience level required. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/NODE-Sudbury/NODE-Sudbury.github.io/blob/HEAD/./CONTRIBUTING.md) for how to get started.

---

## License

Free to use and contribute to. Commercial use is not permitted. See [LICENSE](https://github.com/NODE-Sudbury/NODE-Sudbury.github.io/blob/HEAD/./LICENSE) for details.

projects.description: Front end for Node Events, the Northern Ontario Dev Exchange — a workshops · seminars · hackathons platform.
projects.readme:
# Node Events — UI

Front end for Node Events, the Northern Ontario Dev Exchange — a workshops · seminars · hackathons platform.
**UI only:** there is no backend. All data is mocked in `src/data/mock.js` and any changes you make are persisted to `localStorage` under `node.*` keys.

For a guided  tour (demo logins, test cards, walkthrough) see **[DEMO.md](https://github.com/NODE-Sudbury/NodeEvents/blob/HEAD/DEMO.md)**.

## Run

```bash
npm install
npm run dev        # http://localhost:3000
npm run build && npm start
npm test           # Vitest
npm run lint
```

Deploys to Vercel with no extra configuration (`npm run build` is the build command).
Set `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` in the Vercel project so social link previews use the real domain.

## Stack

Next.js 15 (App Router) · React · JavaScript · CSS Modules · Vitest + Testing Library.
Font: Poppins (300–700) via `next/font`. Event covers are generated gradients — no image assets.

## Routes

| Public | |
|---|---|
| `/` | Marketing home |
| `/discover`, `/discover/[city]` | Browse sessions, city pages |
| `/e/[id]` | Event page + ticket flow (`?register=1` opens it) |
| `/s/[id]` · `/u/[id]` · `/wrapup/[id]` | Series · host profile · post-event wrap-up |
| `/search?q=` | Search results |
| `/signin` | Demo sign-in (persona or any email) |

| Signed in | |
|---|---|
| `/home` | Timeline of events you're attending and hosting |
| `/tickets/[id]` | Ticket pass (QR, cancel) |
| `/e/[id]/team` | Hackathon team project page — submit and edit your project (hackathon events only) |
| `/create` | Create an event |
| `/manage/[id]` | Organizer area: overview, guests, registration, emails, check-in, insights, teams, submissions, judging, settings |
| `/settings` | Profile, notifications, payment methods, demo controls |
| `/sponsor` | Sponsor account |

Old prototype URLs (`/browse`, `/events/:id`, `/dashboard`, …) redirect to their new homes via `next.config.mjs`.

## Structure

```
src/
├── app/                  routes — thin server components rendering feature pages
├── components/
│   ├── layout/           Header, MobileNav, Footer, ScreenIndex (dev screen switcher)
│   └── ui/               Button, Chip, Cover, Field, Modal/Sheet, Dialog, Toast,
│                         Avatar, Stepper, Tabs, CopyField, EmptyState, EventCard…
├── context/              Auth · Registrations · Organizer · App (+ Providers)
├── features/             one folder per screen (event, checkout, home, organizer, …)
├── lib/                  pure logic: tiers, payment, tax, registrationState, dates, cities
├── data/                 mock.js (seed data), personas.js, store.js (localStorage)
└── styles/global.css     design tokens + utility classes
```

## Locale

Everything is written for Canada: Canadian English, prices in Canadian dollars listed before tax, dates month-first (`Fri, Nov 6`, `Nov 6–8`) and times on a 12-hour clock (`5:00 PM`, `Fri 8 PM`).

- **Sales tax** — `src/lib/tax.js` picks the tax from the event's province or territory: 13% HST in Ontario, 5% GST in Nunavut, the Northwest Territories, Yukon and Alberta, 5% GST + 7% PST in British Columbia. Online seats are taxed as Ontario supplies (NODE is based in Ontario). Promo codes come off before tax. Checkout, the receipt and sponsor invoices all price through `priceOrder()` / `taxFor()`.
- **Dates and times** — `src/lib/dates.js` parses the mock `when` / `whenLong` strings and formats clock times (`clock`, `timeRange`, `parseTimeRange`).
- **Money** — `cad()` in `src/utils/format.js` prints whole dollars as `$149` and anything with cents as `$168.37`.

## Design source

`design/` holds the Claude Design canvases the UI was built from — `node-events-original.dc.html` (the design system and first 12 screens) and `node-events-screens.dc.html` (11 product screens), with rendered previews in `design/previews/`.

## Scripts

- `scripts/shot.mjs` — headless-Chrome screenshots with a true mobile viewport
  (`node scripts/shot.mjs --base http://localhost:3000 --out shots --width 390 --height 2400 "/e/rust"`)
- `scripts/e2e-purchase.mjs` — drives the whole ticket purchase with real clicks and screenshots each step
- `scripts/probe.mjs` — quick DOM/localStorage probe for a list of routes

> When using these against `npm start`, don't rebuild `.next` while the server is running — the served chunks 404/400 and the app stops hydrating.

## Docs

- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-19-node-events-product-ui-design.md` — product design spec
- `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-19-wave1-attendee-organizer.md` — implementation plan
- `docs/HANDOFF.md` — state of the build and how work is picked up between sessions

projects.readme:
# grokbot-mocap

Live face motion capture projected onto an animated SVG avatar. Point a camera at a
person and the bot mirrors their head, eyes, blinks and mood in real time. Put a crowd in
front of it and every face gets its own bot on a dark stage.

Built by the NODE Sudbury community for the Grok event. Everything runs in the browser;
no data leaves the machine. MIT licensed, contributions welcome.

**Try it:** https://grokbot-mocap.vercel.app/live

## Running it

Node 22 is required. The repo carries an `.nvmrc`.

```bash
nvm use
pnpm install     # also downloads the MediaPipe models into public/mediapipe/
pnpm dev
```

- http://localhost:5190/live.html — the mirror. Click Start, then **F** fullscreen,
  **H** hide the overlay, **C** hide the camera preview.
- http://localhost:5190/ — the customiser: shape, colour and rest expression, plus an
  animation editor and PNG/SVG/GIF/MP4 export.

```bash
pnpm test     # vitest, ~290 tests, no browser needed
pnpm build    # vue-tsc --noEmit && vite build
```

## What it does

**One person in front of the camera** gets the big bot. Head turns, blinks, wide eyes,
squints and brows are mirrored continuously; a smile, a jaw drop or a frown pulls the
eyes towards the matching expression. Raise a hand and a dock rises: colours on top,
shapes below. Close your fist to grab the cursor, move sideways to pick, up or down to
switch row, open your hand to lock the choice.

**Two to eight people** each get their own bot in a random shape and colour, laid out
like a poster on a night background. Positions follow where people stand. Gestures are
off in crowd mode.

URL switches: `?forme=goutte&couleur=bleu&expression=curieux` presets the single bot,
`?res=720` raises the capture resolution for a far camera, `?demo=5` previews a crowd
scene without a camera, `?worker=0` runs detection on the page thread.

## How it works

- `src/bot/` is the avatar engine: a pure, clock-free `engine.sample(t)` that renders one
  body path and two eye holes from a radial profile and a head pose on a sphere.
- `src/ui/detection.worker.ts` runs MediaPipe's face and hand landmarkers in a Web
  Worker. The page only hands frames over and applies results.
- `src/ui/mirror.ts` turns blendshapes and the head matrix into the engine's levers;
  `poing.ts`, `curseur.ts` and `rangee.ts` read the fist, the hand position and the row;
  `suivi.ts` keeps each person glued to their bot across frames; `scene.ts` places a crowd.
- `src/components/LiveView.vue` is the mirror page; `Dock.vue` and `Foule.vue` the dock
  and the crowd.

Every pure module has tests beside it. See [INSTRUCTIONS.md](https://github.com/NODE-Sudbury/grokbot-mocap/blob/HEAD/INSTRUCTIONS.md) for the
design notes and tuning constants, and [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/NODE-Sudbury/grokbot-mocap/blob/HEAD/CONTRIBUTING.md) to get involved.

## License

MIT. See [LICENSE](https://github.com/NODE-Sudbury/grokbot-mocap/blob/HEAD/LICENSE). Not affiliated with, endorsed by or connected to x.ai;
"Grok" and "x.ai" belong to their owners.
